transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-03-03
Time: 16:00 UTC
Duration: ~62 minutes
Attendees: Alex Chen (Redwood AE), Priya Rao (Redwood SE), Miguel Santos (Redwood), Daniel Carter (Evergrove CISO), Maya Lin (Evergrove Infra), Omar Farouk (Evergrove Cloud Sec), Leah Patel (Evergrove Legal)

[00:00] Alex Chen: Hey everyone, thanks for making time, we'll run through the private VPC security architecture, Priya's gonna walk through the network flows and then we can cover compliance questions. Quick check, is this still the right agenda?
[00:12] Daniel Carter: Yep, that looks good. We're particularly focused on ingress/egress restrictions and KMS integration, and Leah has some legal Qs on data residency.
[00:18] Priya Rao: Great. I'll start with a high-level, then dive into options. So our Private deployment model runs a customer-managed control plane in your VPC, we can do either VPC peering, Transit Gateway, or a dedicated private link depending on the topology and egress policies.
[00:35] Omar Farouk: Quick question - when you say control plane in our VPC, do you mean all components are customer-managed? We need assurance that there is no unintended outbound to internet except allowed endpoints.
[00:45] Priya Rao: Good callout. For the Private VPC we support a fully air-gapped config where egress is blocked except for defined endpoints. In practice we see customers either allow only S3 endpoints and KMS traffic, or put a proxy/NAT with specific allowlist. We can also support no internet egress and bring container images via an internal registry.
[01:05] Miguel Santos: Also worth noting we integrate with customer-managed KMS keys; for highest assurance customers use an HSM-backed CMK. All key operations can be restricted to your KMS and we never persist plaintext model weights or transient request data outside the VPC unless explicitly configured.
[01:24] Maya Lin: On logging, how do you handle audit logs? We need full request traces and per-token cost/latency breakdowns but logs must be exportable to our SIEM and retained for 7 years per policy.
[01:36] Alex Chen: We stream audit logs to a customer-owned S3 or object store via VPC endpoint. Logs include request metadata, model version, latencies, and error traces. Retention is configurable; we can support long-term retention and export hooks to Splunk/Datadog via private endpoints.
[01:52] Daniel Carter: Is there any chance of PII or sensitive data leaving our VPC to Redwood-managed buckets? We cannot allow that.
[02:00] Priya Rao: Understood - default for Private is customer-managed storage only. We can share the runbook that shows the flow: inference nodes -> VPC endpoint -> customer S3/Kinesis behind VPC endpoint. We do have an option for a managed bucket with strict controls but for Evergrove we'd recommend customer-owned.
[02:20] Leah Patel: Legally we need to see SOC 2 and ISO27001 attestations and the last external penetration test. Can you provide redacted reports?
[02:29] Alex Chen: Yes, we'll send SOC2 Type II and ISO27001 scope plus a pen-test summary. We'll redact as needed. I'll include contacts for security/edu.
[02:38] Omar Farouk: For network controls, can we see a sample security group/NACL configuration? We want explicit deny-by-default with allow rules only to KMS endpoints, internal monitoring, and our SIEM.
[02:50] Priya Rao: Absolutely. Common config: private subnets for inference nodes, no public IPs, egress via proxy/NAT with strict allowlist, VPC Endpoint for KMS, S3 gateway endpoints, and security group rules that only allow traffic from the control-plane subnets and your management CIDRs. We can also front with an NGFW (Palo Alto/Checkpoint) in a centralized inspection tier if you require DPI.
[03:12] Miguel Santos: On the ingress side, we support either private load balancers with customer ingress VPC endpoints, or mutual TLS tunnels from your edge. If you need zero public ingress, we use AWS PrivateLink or internal ALBs.
[03:27] Maya Lin: Latency is a concern - if we put an NGFW inline that does heavy inspection, will Redwood's latency SLOs be impacted?
[03:33] Priya Rao: It depends on placement. We recommend putting lightweight L4 rules in path and offload DPI to a side-channel or a regional inspection cluster. Redwood's runtime can be co-located to minimize intra-VPC hops; we can provide sample benchmarking for your expected QPS.
[03:51] Daniel Carter: About RBAC and SSO - we use Okta and SAML. Can you integrate for admin access and support scoped service accounts for operators?
[03:59] Alex Chen: Yes, we support SAML SSO via IdP and SCIM for user provisioning. For RBAC we provide roles mapped to Okta groups; admin operations, read-only, and deploy roles are available. For API-level keys we also support short-lived tokens minted via your IdP.
[04:18] Omar Farouk: KMS question - can we keep keys in our HSM cluster? We use an external HSM for key custody and require that no key material be exportable.
[04:26] Miguel Santos: We support customer-owned KMS including HSM-backed CMKs (AWS CloudHSM, etc.). Key usage is limited to cryptographic operations; private keys never leave your HSM. We can also integrate via PKCS#11 if needed for on-prem HSM.
[04:41] Maya Lin: Data residency - some workflows must remain in our EU region. Can Redwood ensure the inference nodes and logs are kept in eu-west-1 and never leave that region?
[04:50] Priya Rao: Yes, deployments are region-pinned. For Private we can deploy the control plane and inference nodes in your chosen region and the default behavior is no cross-region replication unless you opt into it. We'll document the data flow in the runbook.
[05:06] Daniel Carter: Are there any shared management networks that other customers can reach? We need assurance of tenant isolation.
[05:12] Alex Chen: For Private deployments, the control plane lives in your VPC or in a dedicated VPC peered only to your account depending on the pattern. There's no shared tenant routing across customers. We can also provide network-level microsegmentation examples.
[05:27] Leah Patel: For audits, do you provide access to raw audit logs and a timeline of config changes for three years?
[05:34] Alex Chen: Yes, we provide immutable append-only logs shipped to your S3 with versioning and MFA-delete options. We also can provide a change history for deployments and rollouts that maps to user identities via SSO.
[05:48] Miguel Santos: For firewalling, customers commonly choose one of three patterns: 1) Simple security group + NAT allowlist, 2) Transit Gateway + centralized NGFW for inspection, or 3) Air-gapped with curated egress via internal artifact repo and no internet at all. We can share reference IaC for each.
[06:07] Omar Farouk: In the Transit GW setup, how do you manage route table changes during canary rollouts to prevent accidental exposure?
[06:13] Priya Rao: We rely on a deployment orchestration that uses explicit ephemeral route tables and automated rollback if any egress rule violates the allowlist. We'll share the orchestration flow - it's in the runbook draft.
[06:26] Maya Lin: Any limitations on model sizes or KV cache storage with Private? We have some large models and we need to know footprint for subnet planning.
[06:34] Miguel Santos: Model weights are kept on local NVMe attached to inference nodes; we recommend capacity planning based on model footprint. We'll provide an example spreadsheet mapping model sizes to node types and subnet/min IP counts.
[06:49] Daniel Carter: Ok, sounds good. Let's talk about the pilot: we want a small dedicated cluster in our eu-west-1 with HSM-backed KMS, no internet egress, logs to our S3, and SSO for operator access. Timeline is roughly 6-8 weeks to pilot.
[07:05] Alex Chen: That aligns with what we've done before. Proposed immediate actions: I'll send compliance artifacts and the runbook; Priya will draft a VPC reference architecture and Miguel will produce capacity estimate. Omar, you'll share the current network diagram.
[07:20] Omar Farouk: I'll send the diagram and blocked egress list by Friday.
[07:24] Leah Patel: Also please include data processing addendum and DPA language for logs and incident response.
[07:30] Alex Chen: Noted - we'll include DPA and incident response contacts.
[07:33] Priya Rao: Anything else on the architecture side?
[07:36] Maya Lin: No, that's it for now. We'll review the docs and then schedule a walkthrough of the runbook next week.
[07:42] Alex Chen: Great thanks everyone, recap in follow-up email with attachments.
[07:45] Miguel Santos: Thanks all.

Meeting end.
